spec_match.rationale: The scripted narrative uses navigator.modelContext.tools and navigator.modelContext.callTool(name, args), neither of which exists. The spec flow is document.modelContext.getTools({fromOrigins}) returning Tool objects (name/title/description/inputSchema/source/origin) and executeTool(tool, input, {signal}) resolving to a DOMString, plus toolactivated/toolcancel events. None of it is called, even with the flag on.

interactive.rationale: Three scenarios step through to completion (8/9/6 steps verified) and Reset works, but every message is canned text.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Matches the index blurb's step-through, but the 'Origin Trial simulation' note and 'faithful simulation of navigator.modelContext' are inaccurate.

edge_cases.rationale: Includes a tool-not-found scenario, but not executeTool rejection, cancellation via AbortSignal/toolcancel, cross-origin exposedTo/fromOrigins discovery, or a consequential-action confirmation. The claim that 'inputs are validated against inputSchema before the handler runs' is not stated in the spec algorithms reviewed (executeTool only JSON-serialises the input).

references.rationale: Cites chromestatus 5117755740913664 and modelcontextprotocol.io, but not the WebMCP spec.

conformance.rationale: Every assertion in the feature suite passes vacuously when WebMCP is absent: on default Chromium 157 (no document.modelContext) the suite reads 6/6 PASS, and 'registertool-rejects-tool-without-name' passes only because document.modelContext is undefined (TypeError on property access). Nothing exercises getTools(), executeTool(), name validation, duplicate-name InvalidStateError or AbortSignal unregistration.

runtime_evidence.rationale: All three scenarios were stepped to the end and reset at both viewports with 0 console errors and 0 failed requests. chrome-devtools-mcp is not available in this environment, so this is NOT DevTools-MCP verification (rule 7b); evidence is Playwright headless Chromium 157.0.8103.78 at 1280x800 and 360x740 DPR3 touch.

telemetry_health.rationale: The shared /public/demo-telemetry.js is injected (runtime/resource errors would be captured) but the page emits no page-specific assertion or interaction events, and /telemetry/demo/events (Basic auth) was not queried in this pass.

design_system.rationale: Uses variables; the active scenario is distinguished only by inverted colours, and inline styles are scattered through the markup.

accessibility.rationale: Native buttons, but the annotation that explains each step has no aria-live (verified null), scenario buttons expose no aria-pressed (verified), and the active/done step state is a CSS class only. Accessibility tree not inspected with chrome-devtools-mcp (unavailable).

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No page-level overflow at 360x740 and the arena stacks, but 4 of 5 controls are under 44px tall.

openQuestions.title: Replace origin-trial framing with the real flag steps
openQuestions.detail: ChromeStatus records no origin trial for 5117755740913664 (status 'Proposed', flag 'Experimental Web Platform features' / finch 'WebMCP'). Verified on Chromium 157: document.modelContext appears with --enable-features=WebMCP, --enable-blink-features=WebMCP or --enable-experimental-web-platform-features, and navigator.modelContext is never exposed. Pages variously claim an 'Origin Trial (Chrome 149-156)' token, 'navigator.mcpServer with the WebMCP flag', or a 146 flag. Banner should give chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features, --enable-blink-features=WebMCP and --enable-features=WebMCP, note [SecureContext], and match across all four concepts and the feature index (rule 10).

openQuestions.title: Rewrite the protocol sequence to the spec surface
openQuestions.detail: Replace .tools/callTool with await document.modelContext.getTools() and await document.modelContext.executeTool(tool, input, {signal}). Note that executeTool resolves to a string and that the page's execute callback receives {signal}.

openQuestions.title: Add a live handshake concept that really calls getTools/executeTool
openQuestions.detail: Keep this simulator as-is (additive contract) and add a concept that, with the WebMCP flag, registers two tools, discovers them with getTools(), executes one with executeTool(), shows toolactivated/toolcancel events, and cancels a slow tool via AbortController. Verified on Chromium 157 + flag: getTools/executeTool round-trip returns the execute callback's JSON string.

openQuestions.title: Announce step annotations and expose scenario state
openQuestions.detail: Put the annotation in a polite live region, give scenario buttons aria-pressed, and expose the current step as text (e.g. aria-current on the active step).

openQuestions.title: Flag for a human: WebMCP conformance suite passes vacuously and asserts sync throw for a promise API
openQuestions.detail: Conformance is immutable, so this is a human decision. On Chromium 157 without the flag the suite reads 6/6 PASS with no document.modelContext; the 'throws' assertion for a nameless tool only passes because the property access throws. In the spec registerTool returns a Promise and a missing required dictionary member becomes a rejected promise (verified with the flag: the promise rejects with TypeError), so a synchronous-throw contract is the wrong shape. Additive assertions for getTools()/executeTool(), name-charset InvalidStateError, duplicate-name InvalidStateError and AbortSignal unregistration (all verified behaviourally on Chromium 157 + WebMCP flag) would make the suite meaningful.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify with chrome-devtools-mcp (Canary + WebMCP flag) and inspect the accessibility tree
openQuestions.detail: This pass used Playwright headless Chromium 157 because chrome-devtools-mcp was unavailable; repeat the control walk, console/network check and accessibility-tree inspection through the MCP per rule 7b.

guidanceConsulted.query: live region announcing dynamic log output
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce dynamically changing status/log output through an appropriate live region or <output>, keep native semantics and associated labels for controls.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review only: the page's changing readouts carry no aria-live/role=status; recorded as an open question.

guidanceConsulted.query: toggle button group aria-pressed selected state
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use native buttons for actions and expose selected/toggled state (aria-pressed or radio semantics) instead of class-only visual state.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review only: preset/scenario selectors expose selection only via a CSS class; recorded as an open question.

guidanceConsulted.query: minimum touch target size for buttons on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep touch targets usable (~44px) and content within its space on narrow viewports.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review only: measured controls below 44px tall at 360x740; recorded under mobile_desktop_parity.

summary: A well-written narrative stepper with three scenarios that works and has a clean console. The protocol it narrates (navigator.modelContext.tools / callTool) is not the WebMCP spec, it never calls the real document.modelContext even when the flag exposes it, and its step annotations are not announced. Verified with Playwright headless Chromium 157, not chrome-devtools-mcp.
